title: Contratto Bitter Liqueur
about: Contratto is one of the historic houses of Canelli, the Piedmont town that gave Italy its sparkling Moscato. Giuseppe Contratto founded the firm in 1867, and beginning in 1899 the company spent about ten years hand-digging cellars more than thirty metres into the hillside beneath its headquarters, part of the “underground cathedrals” of Canelli now within the UNESCO-listed vineyard landscape of Piedmont. Since 2011 Contratto has belonged to Giorgio Rivetti and his brothers of La Spinetta, who revived the aperitivi and digestivi the house had stopped making in the late 1960s.

The Bitter follows a recipe the label dates to 1933. Twenty-four herbs, spices, roots and seeds go into it, among them aloe, bitter and sweet orange, wormwood, clove, cardamom, gentian, hibiscus, elecampane, juniper, mint, rhubarb, sage and nettle. As with the house’s other aperitivi, the botanicals are hammer-milled and cold-macerated for more than thirty-five days, blended with an organic Italian wheat distillate from Cuneo, sweetened with beet sugar and coloured naturally with carrot and beetroot. After chilling and slow filtration it rests in stainless steel before bottling at 22% alcohol.

With 200 grams of sugar per litre it is drier than the house’s Aperitif. Its importer calls it an intuitive replacement for Campari, one that brings depth without severity or any artificial note on the finish, and suggests it for a bold spritz or a fruit-forward Negroni, stirred with gin and sweet vermouth and served over ice.
